editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the key caveat in [10]: update_tags() overwrites existing tags, so the original tags have to be re-assigned. Entry [10] has two small wording problems. It calls the API method "`update_tags()` na paraan" and then "pamamaraang ito" in the next sentence, so one method gets two names. It also uses the causative "Pina-overwrite", where a native writer would say "Ino-overwrite" or "Pinapalitan".

examples.source: This method overwrites current tags
examples.translation: Pina-overwrite ng pamamaraang ito ang mga kasalukuyang tag
examples.suggested: Ino-overwrite ng method na ito ang mga kasalukuyang tag
examples.why: The causative prefix pina- reads as 'causes to be overwritten', which is a stiff calque. Ino-overwrite is the natural actor-less form.

examples.source: with the `update_tags()` method. This method ...
examples.translation: gamit ang `update_tags()` na paraan. ... pamamaraang ito
examples.suggested: gamit ang `update_tags()` method. ... Ang method na ito
examples.why: The same API method is called 'paraan' and then 'pamamaraan' two sentences apart. 'Paraan' also reads as 'way/manner', not a programming method. Keeping 'method' would be clearer and consistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The region caveat in [16] ("makikita at maa-access mo lang ang mga instance na nilikha sa rehiyong naka-log in ka") and the profile-is-not-your-account note in [12] both keep their restrictions. There are two small things an editor would change. 'Credentials' is kept as English 'access credential' in the heading [18] but becomes Tagalog 'kredensyal' in the next sentence [19]. Also, the Python method in [19] is called "`save_account()` na paraan", where 'paraan' reads as 'way/manner', not a programming method.

examples.source: it is recommended that you use the `save_account()` method to [save your credentials locally]
examples.translation: inirerekomenda na gamitin ang `save_account()` na paraan para [i-save ang iyong mga kredensyal nang lokal]
examples.suggested: inirerekomenda na gamitin ang `save_account()` method para [i-save ang iyong mga credential nang lokal]
examples.why: The heading [18] keeps 'credential' in English but the sentence right below it switches to 'kredensyal'. Pick one and use it throughout the page. 'paraan' is also a loose word for a code method, and developer-facing Tagalog usually keeps 'method'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner. The steps, the caveats in [28] (Public Access group) and [30] (all resources) and the role list all match the English. There are two small slips. The sample description in [24] uses the ungrammatical "maaari kang tingnan" where Tagalog needs the actor-focus pronoun "maaari mong tingnan". In [30], "scope the access to all resources" becomes "ililimitahan ang access sa lahat ng resources", and "limit to all" reads awkwardly for what is really a widening of scope.

examples.source: As an Analytics Viewer, you can view account analytics only.
examples.translation: Bilang isang Analytics Viewer, maaari kang tingnan ang analytics ng account lamang.
examples.suggested: Bilang isang Analytics Viewer, maaari mo lamang tingnan ang analytics ng account.
examples.why: 'maaari kang' + object-focus verb 'tingnan' is ungrammatical. It needs the genitive 'mo', and placing 'lamang' right after the modal reads more naturally.

examples.source: if you do not scope the access to all resources
examples.translation: kung hindi mo ililimitahan ang access sa lahat ng resources
examples.suggested: kung hindi mo itatakda ang saklaw ng access sa lahat ng resources

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The 90%/80% mitigation thresholds in [31]-[33], the "does not mutate two-qubit gates, number of qubits, or circuit depth" caveat in [18] and the "less severe than a real QPU" caution in [25] all come through correctly. There are a few small slips. In [34], "will hopefully improve" becomes the more confident "malamang na magpapabuti". In [9] and [18], "efficient simulation" becomes "mas mahusay na simulation" ("better" simulation) instead of "mas episyenteng". Some phrasing is calqued, such as "wrapper sa paligid ng" in [18] and "Ang mga simulate na resulta" in [24].

examples.source: applying PEA to the original circuit will hopefully improve the quality of its results
examples.translation: ang pag-apply ng PEA sa orihinal na circuit ay malamang na magpapabuti ng kalidad ng mga resulta nito
examples.suggested: ang pag-apply ng PEA sa orihinal na circuit ay sana'y magpapabuti ng kalidad ng mga resulta nito
examples.why: 'Hopefully' is a hedge, and 'malamang' (likely) makes the claim a bit stronger than the English. The difference is small, so it does not mislead.

examples.source: map them to Clifford circuits for more efficient simulation
examples.translation: i-map ang mga ito sa mga Clifford circuit para sa mas mahusay na simulation
examples.suggested: i-map ang mga ito sa mga Clifford circuit para sa mas episyenteng simulation
examples.why: 'Mahusay' means better or skilled. The point here is computational efficiency (Clifford circuits are cheap to simulate classically), so 'episyente' says it more precisely. The same wording appears in [9].

examples.source: is a wrapper around the ConvertISAToClifford transpiler pass
examples.translation: ay isang wrapper sa paligid ng ConvertISAToClifford transpiler pass
examples.suggested: ay isang wrapper ng ConvertISAToClifford transpiler pass
examples.why: 'Sa paligid ng' is a literal calque of 'around' and reads stiffly. A native writer would just say 'wrapper ng'.

examples.source: The simulated results support mathematical operations
examples.translation: Ang mga simulate na resulta ay sumusuporta sa mga mathematical na operasyon
examples.suggested: Puwedeng gamitan ng mga mathematical na operasyon ang mga resulta ng simulation
examples.why: 'Simulate na resulta' is a calque of 'simulated results', and the inverted 'ay' construction plus 'sumusuporta' reads like machine translation.

editor_note: The meaning matches the English throughout. The defaults (sabre, translator, alap, approximation 1.0), the override rules and the notes that only optimization_level is required and that the final layout is not guaranteed all carry over correctly. The problems are wording. In [42], "greedily" becomes "nang masigasig" ("diligently"), so the greedy-scheduling sense of ASAP is lost. There are several calques and grammar slips: "sa gastos ng" for "at the expense of" [17], "maaaring makaka-apekto" and "ang value na iyon ay ino-override ang lahat ng pass" [29], and the past-tense "direktang ipinasa" where the sense is habitual [31, 34]. Entry [22] also drops "control" from "control hardware restriction".

examples.source: Schedule instructions greedily, as early as possible
examples.translation: I-schedule ang mga instruction nang masigasig, nang maaga hangga't maaari
examples.suggested: I-schedule ang mga instruction nang greedy (sakim), nang maaga hangga't maaari
examples.why: 'masigasig' means diligent/zealous, not the algorithmic 'greedy' strategy; the technical sense is lost.

examples.source: Some of them might impact multiple stages ... that value overrides all the passes that could change it.
examples.translation: Ang ilan sa mga ito ay maaaring makaka-apekto sa maraming yugto ... ang value na iyon ay ino-override ang lahat ng pass na maaaring baguhin ito.
examples.suggested: Ang ilan sa mga ito ay maaaring makaapekto sa maraming yugto ... ino-override ng value na iyon ang lahat ng pass na maaaring magbago rito.
examples.why: 'maaaring makaka-apekto' is ungrammatical (double modal/aspect) and the ay-inversion with an actor-focus verb reads as a calque.

examples.source: at the expense of longer transpilation time
examples.translation: sa gastos ng mas matagal na transpilation time
examples.suggested: kapalit ng mas matagal na transpilation time
examples.why: 'sa gastos ng' is a literal calque of 'at the expense of'; 'kapalit ng' is the natural idiom.

examples.source: that is passed directly to the HighLevelSynthesis transformation pass
examples.translation: na direktang ipinasa sa HighLevelSynthesis transformation pass
examples.suggested: na direktang ipinapasa sa HighLevelSynthesis transformation pass
examples.why: Completed aspect 'ipinasa' implies a past event; the habitual/general 'ipinapasa' fits a parameter description (same in [34]).

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: shot counts (1024, 1000), 900 randomizations, task indices and the Twirl/InjectNoise split all match the English. Entry [40] translates the idiom "up to single-qubit gates" literally as "hanggang sa single-qubit na gate", which reads as "until", and it uses "pantay" (level/even) for "equal". The uniqueness rule comes through blurred but not inverted. "Execute" is rendered three ways (Isabuhay in the headings and steps, Isakatuparan in [27], patakbuhin elsewhere), and "Isabuhay" is an odd choice for running code. Some smaller calques: "tagubilin" is used for ISA/box instructions ([14], [40]), "Minsan… at minsan" in [29], and "katulad ng" for "namely" in [41], which makes the list sound incomplete.

examples.source: Their content is equal, up to single-qubit gates.
examples.translation: Ang kanilang nilalaman ay pantay, hanggang sa single-qubit na gate.
examples.suggested: Magkapareho ang kanilang nilalaman kung hindi isasaalang-alang ang mga single-qubit gate.
examples.why: 'hanggang sa' means 'until', so it carries over the English idiom without its mathematical sense ('ignoring differences in'), and 'pantay' means level/even, not identical. The equivalence rule becomes unclear to a learner.

examples.source: 3. Execute: Add a circuit item and a samplex item ... and execute both in a single job.
examples.translation: 3. Isabuhay: Magdagdag ng circuit item ...
examples.suggested: 3. Patakbuhin: ...
examples.why: 'Isabuhay' (bring to life / put into practice) is an unnatural word for running code. 'Execute' also appears as Isakatuparan in [27] and patakbuhin elsewhere; use one term consistently.

examples.source: Once with only Pauli-twirling applied, and once withe PEC mitigation applied.
examples.translation: Minsan na may Pauli-twirling lamang na inilapat, at minsan na may PEC mitigation na inilapat.
examples.suggested: Isang beses na Pauli-twirling lamang ang inilapat, at isang beses na may PEC mitigation.
examples.why: 'Minsan' usually reads as 'sometimes', which weakens the idea of exactly two runs. The phrasing is also a calque.

examples.source: This leads to three unique instructions, namely the odd and even gate boxes, and the final measurement box.
examples.translation: ... katulad ng odd at even na gate box, at ang panghuling measurement box.
examples.suggested: ... ito ay ang odd at even na gate box, at ang panghuling measurement box.
examples.why: 'katulad ng' means 'such as', which suggests the list is incomplete. 'namely' lists all three exactly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The editable-mode caveat about rebuilding with `build_rust` in [32] comes through intact. examples.source: inspect and extend the latest version of the Qiskit code more efficiently

examples.suggested: mas mabilis at madali mong masusuri at mapapalawak

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. In [3], the tip still says to create instances before inviting users. In [16], the note still says removed users lose visibility of their workloads while other users in the instance keep access. Two small wording fixes remain. [10] spells the verb 'in-imbitahang', which should be 'inimbitahang'. examples.suggested: opsyonal na italaga ang mga inimbitahang gumagamit sa mga access group

examples.source: select the access groups the user should belong to

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. examples.source: Users are defined in IBM Cloud and project assignments are done there as well.

examples.source: To manage ID provider users instead, follow the instructions in the [Manage ID providers] topic.

examples.source: Review [Leclerc, L., et al. (2023)...]

examples.source: but the already submitted jobs will still run until completion
examples.translation: ngunit ang mga naisumiiteng job ay patuloy na tatakbo hanggang matapos

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The contrast between the e-bit and shared randomness, the Bell state and the unentangled probabilistic state (2) all come through correctly, and the terms are used consistently (entanglement, qubit, state, e-bit). A native editor would still fix a few slips. "Ang 'e' ay nakatayo para sa" is a word-for-word copy of the English "stands for". "Para sa breviedad" uses a word that doesn't exist in Tagalog. In [20], "somehow" became "sa anumang paraan" ("in any way"). In [21], the grammar of "kung paano kumakatawan ang ating kaalaman" makes it say "how our knowledge represents" when the English means how we represent our knowledge.

examples.source: The "e" stands for "entangled" or "entanglement."
examples.translation: Ang "e" ay nakatayo para sa "entangled" o "entanglement."
examples.suggested: Ang "e" ay nangangahulugang "entangled" o "entanglement."
examples.why: "Nakatayo para sa" copies the English idiom "stands for" word for word (it literally means "is standing for"). Tagalog would say "nangangahulugang" or "kumakatawan sa".

examples.source: for the sake of brevity
examples.translation: para sa breviedad
examples.suggested: para sa kaiklian
examples.why: "Breviedad" is not a Tagalog word, and it isn't correct Spanish either (that would be "brevedad"). The Tagalog word is "kaiklian".

examples.source: the state of the other qubit is somehow instantaneously affected
examples.translation: ang state ng isa pang qubit ay agad na naaapektuhan sa anumang paraan
examples.suggested: ang state ng isa pang qubit ay kung paanuman ay agad na naaapektuhan
examples.why: "Sa anumang paraan" means "in any way", which loses the vague, mysterious sense of "somehow" in the English. It is a small shift and does not reverse the claim.

examples.source: the decisions we make about how to represent our knowledge of states using vectors
examples.translation: kung paano kumakatawan ang ating kaalaman ng mga state gamit ang mga vector
examples.suggested: kung paano natin kinakatawan ang ating kaalaman tungkol sa mga state gamit ang mga vector
examples.why: The verb form makes "our knowledge" the one doing the representing, so the Tagalog reads as "how our knowledge represents". The English means we are the ones who represent our knowledge.

examples.source: Incidentally, we can also view the probabilistic state (2) as a resource
examples.translation: Sa puntong ito, maaari rin nating tingnan
examples.suggested: Siyanga pala, maaari rin nating tingnan
examples.why: "Sa puntong ito" means "at this point", which drops the sense of a side remark that "Incidentally" carries.

editor_note: In the Unitary operations section and everything after it, "classical state set" is repeatedly shortened to "klasikal na estado" (classical state), which drops the idea of a set. The result misleads: [206] now says X and Y "are in the same classical state Σ" instead of sharing the same state set, [213] says R has "whatever classical state we wish" instead of any state set, and [164]/[194] give a system a single "classical state Σ". Terminology also splits across the page. The first half uses "quantum state" / "classical state set", the middle uses "quantum na estado" / "classical na hanay ng mga estado", and the last part uses "klasikal na estado". Measurement becomes "sukat sa standard na batayan" ("sukat" usually means size), and the basis states later become "standard basis state". There are also calques and grammar slips: "Maaari tayong gamitin" ([8]), "sa pamamagitan ng paraan" for "by the way" ([194]), "iniwan nang walang bago" ([129]), "nakakabit" for "interspersed" ([130]), and "tamang subset" for proper subset ([72]).

examples.source: Suppose that X and Y are systems that share the same classical state set Σ.
examples.translation: Ipagpalagay na ang X at Y ay mga sistema na may parehong klasikal na estado na Σ.
examples.suggested: Ipagpalagay na ang X at Y ay mga sistema na may parehong classical state set na Σ.
examples.why: Changes 'share the same state set' into 'have the same classical state'. A learner would read this as the two systems being in the same state, which is a false premise for SWAP.

examples.source: R is an arbitrary system, having whatever classical state set we wish.
examples.translation: ang R ay isang arbitrary na sistema, na may anumang klasikal na estado na nais natin.
examples.suggested: ang R ay isang arbitrary na sistema, na may anumang classical state set na nais natin.
examples.why: Says R can be in any state we choose, when the English means R can have any state set (qubit, qutrit, and so on). This teaches the wrong generality for controlled-U.

examples.source: if X is a system having classical state set Σ ... then the classical state set of the joint system (X,Y) is Σ×Γ
examples.translation: kung ang X ay isang sistema na may klasikal na estado na Σ ... ang klasikal na estado ng joint system na (X,Y) ay Σ×Γ
examples.suggested: kung ang X ay isang sistema na may classical state set na Σ ... ang classical state set ng joint system na (X,Y) ay Σ×Γ
examples.why: Treats a set of states as a single state. This conflicts with the earlier correct 'classical state set' rendering and hides why unitary rows and columns are indexed by Σ×Γ.

examples.source: Standard basis measurements of quantum states of single systems
examples.translation: mga sukat sa standard na batayan ng mga quantum na estado ng mga indibidwal na sistema ... classical na hanay ng mga estado
examples.suggested: mga standard basis measurement ng mga quantum state ... classical state set (consistent with [4]-[64])
examples.why: From here on, 'quantum state', 'classical state set' and 'measurement' switch to different renderings from the first half, so the same concepts look like new terms.

examples.source: We may use the fact that ...
examples.translation: Maaari tayong gamitin ang katotohanan na ...
examples.suggested: Maaari nating gamitin ang katotohanan na ...
examples.why: Wrong pronoun form for an object-focus verb. The same slip appears in [26] ('maaari tayong sundin') and [59] ('maaari rin tayong isaalang-alang').

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the 5/9 vs 4/9 (556/444) sampling example, the global-phase caveat ('katumbas maliban sa isang global phase') and the run-sequentially note all match the English. A few spots read stiffly. Entry [37] calques 'more and more / closer and closer' as 'mas marami at mas maraming… mas malapit at mas malapit', and it spells 'fenomenong' where Tagalog uses 'penomenong'. Entry [12] renders 'leaves something to be desired' as the awkward 'may kung ano mang kulang, sa visual na paraan'. Entry [4] slightly reframes 'the quantum computers it is used to operate' as 'na ginagamit nito' (which the computers use), which is imprecise but does not mislead.

examples.source: With more and more samples, the fraction of samples for each possibility is likely to get closer and closer to the corresponding probability. This phenomenon...
examples.translation: Sa mas marami at mas maraming sample, ... ay malamang na magiging mas malapit at mas malapit sa katumbas na posibilidad. Ang fenomenong ito...
examples.suggested: Habang dumarami ang sample, malamang na lalong lumalapit ang fraction ng bawat posibilidad sa katumbas nitong probability. Ang penomenong ito...
examples.why: Literal calque of the English doubling construction; 'fenomenong' is a Spanish-style spelling (Tagalog: 'penomenong').

examples.source: This output formatting leaves something to be desired, visually speaking.
examples.translation: Ang output formatting na ito ay may kung ano mang kulang, sa visual na paraan.
examples.suggested: Hindi gaanong maganda tingnan ang output formatting na ito.
examples.why: Word-for-word rendering of an English idiom; reads as MT.

examples.source: the quantum computers it is used to operate
examples.translation: ng mga quantum computer na ginagamit nito
examples.suggested: ng mga quantum computer na pinapatakbo gamit ito
examples.why: 'na ginagamit nito' reads as 'which it uses' rather than 'which it is used to operate'. The subject/object relation is slightly off, but the reader is not misled.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few small slips. In [16], the ongoing "are shared" became the completed "ibinahagi". In [20], "enabling adoption" became "pagpapahintulot", which means granting permission rather than making something possible. In [18], "nasubok sa larangan ng mga partner" can read as "tested in the partners' field". [23] uses the odd form "natatag" for "established", and [29] has the misspelling "nagstandarize".

examples.source: select channels where the latest ideas in quantum are shared
examples.translation: mga piling channel kung saan ibinahagi ang pinakabagong mga ideya sa quantum
examples.suggested: mga piling channel kung saan ibinabahagi ang pinakabagong mga ideya sa quantum
examples.why: The completed-aspect verb 'ibinahagi' turns an ongoing, habitual sharing into a one-time past event. The English means sharing happens continually.

examples.source: by enabling enterprise-grade adoption at a global scale
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahintulot ng enterprise-grade na pag-adopt
examples.suggested: sa pamamagitan ng pagpapadali/pagsasakatuparan ng enterprise-grade na pag-adopt
examples.why: 'Pagpapahintulot' means granting permission, but 'enabling' here means making something possible or facilitating it.

examples.source: were developed and field-tested by partners in the IBM Quantum Network
examples.translation: ay binuo at nasubok sa larangan ng mga partner sa IBM Quantum Network
examples.suggested: ay binuo at sinubok sa aktuwal na paggamit ng mga partner sa IBM Quantum Network
examples.why: This literal calque of 'field-tested' can be misread as 'tested in the partners' field', which hides the meaning of 'tested in practice'.

examples.source: Enterprise organizations are established companies
examples.translation: ay mga natatag na kumpanya
examples.suggested: ay mga matagal nang itinatag na kumpanya
examples.why: 'Natatag' is an unnatural form. 'Matagal nang itinatag' or 'matatag' conveys 'established' properly.

examples.source: standardizes shared tooling
examples.translation: nagstandarize ng shared tooling
examples.suggested: nag-i-standardize ng shared tooling
examples.why: Both the English root and the Tagalog affixing are misspelled. Standard Taglish orthography uses a hyphenated 'nag-i-standardize'.

editor_note: Entry [55] gets a number wrong. "When p is larger than one-half" became "mas malaki sa isa't kalahati", which means "larger than one and a half". That misstates the classical break-even point that [68] later gives as 50%, so this alone is a FAIL. There are also some smaller slips. In [19], "hereafter" became "sa ngayon" ("for now"). In [68], "brilliant discovery" became "magiting na natuklasan" ("heroic/brave"). There are two calques: "sa pamamagitan ng paraan" for "by the way" in [53], and "apat na mas kaunting" in [33]. And [20] has the wrong pronoun in "maaari tayong tratuhin".

examples.source: just like the 3-bit repetition code is worse than no code when $p$ is larger than one-half.
examples.translation: tulad ng 3-bit repetition code na mas masahol kaysa sa walang code kapag ang $p$ ay mas malaki sa isa't kalahati.
examples.suggested: tulad ng 3-bit repetition code na mas masahol pa kaysa sa walang code kapag ang $p$ ay mas malaki sa kalahati.
examples.why: 'isa't kalahati' means 1.5, not 1/2. This changes the threshold being taught and contradicts the 50% break-even point in [68].

examples.source: which we'll generally refer to as $X$ errors hereafter for the sake of brevity.
examples.translation: na sa ngayon ay tatawaging $X$ error para sa ikli.
examples.suggested: na mula ngayon ay karaniwan nating tatawaging $X$ error para maikli.
examples.why: 'sa ngayon' means 'for now / temporarily', but the English means 'from here on'. The word 'generally' is also dropped.

examples.source: the 9-qubit Shor code represents a brilliant discovery
examples.translation: kumakatawan sa isang magiting na natuklasan
examples.suggested: kumakatawan sa isang napakahusay na tuklas
examples.why: 'magiting' means brave or heroic, which is the wrong word for a brilliant discovery. 'pati na rin' is also used twice in the same sentence.

examples.source: A $Y$ error, by the way, is equivalent
examples.translation: Ang isang $Y$ error, sa pamamagitan ng paraan, ay katumbas
examples.suggested: Siyanga pala, ang isang $Y$ error ay katumbas
examples.why: This translates 'by the way' word for word into 'by means of the way', which no native writer would use.

examples.source: we can simply treat each of the three blocks in the encoding separately.
examples.translation: maaari tayong tratuhin ang bawat isa sa tatlong bloke
examples.suggested: maaari lang nating tratuhin nang hiwalay ang bawat isa sa tatlong bloke
examples.why: A transitive verb with a patient focus needs 'nating', not 'tayong'. 'simply' is also dropped.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the noise-model caveats, the "logical qubits are never exposed" point and the threshold/break-even argument, and the terms are used consistently (noise model, gadget, logical/pisikal na qubit). A native editor would still fix a few calques and slips. In [22], "naitatayo ang entropy" uses the word for building a structure where it should say entropy accumulates. [23] switches from inclusive "natin" to exclusive "kami/naming" in the middle of a sentence. In [24], "ang buong prosesong iminungkahi lamang" reads as "the process only suggested" rather than "just suggested", and "gumagawa ng mga bagay na mas masahol pa" is stiff.

examples.source: As errors take place, entropy builds up
examples.translation: Habang nagaganap ang mga error, naitatayo ang entropy
examples.suggested: Habang nagaganap ang mga error, naiipon ang entropy
examples.why: 'itayo' means to erect a structure. It is a calque of 'build up', and 'naiipon' or 'dumarami' says accumulation.

examples.source: there is a fundamental question that we may ask ourselves
examples.translation: mayroon kaming pundamental na tanong na maaari naming itanong sa ating sarili
examples.suggested: may pundamental na tanong na maaari nating itanong sa ating sarili
examples.why: The exclusive 'kami/naming' shuts the learner out and clashes with the 'ating' in the same clause. The rest of the page uses the inclusive 'natin'.

examples.source: the entire process just suggested could very well be making things worse
examples.translation: ang buong prosesong iminungkahi lamang ay maaaring gumagawa ng mga bagay na mas masahol pa
examples.suggested: ang buong prosesong kalalarawan pa lang ay maaaring lalo pang nagpapalala ng sitwasyon
examples.why: 'iminungkahi lamang' can be read as 'merely suggested' instead of 'just described'. 'gumagawa ng mga bagay na mas masahol pa' is a literal calque.

examples.source: these classical computations can safely be assumed to be perfect as well
examples.translation: ang mga klasikal na computation na ito ay maaari ring ipalagay na perpekto
examples.suggested: ligtas ding maipapalagay na perpekto ang mga klasikal na computation na ito
examples.why: The qualifier 'safely' is dropped, which weakens the justification slightly. It does not mislead.

editor_note: Two key concepts are mistranslated in ways that would mislead a learner. In [68], measuring stabilizer generators "non-destructively" becomes "nang hindi mapanganib" ("not dangerously"), which loses the idea of a measurement that doesn't destroy the encoded state. In [75], Steane error correction's core idea, "intentionally propagate errors to a workspace system", becomes "sadya nating pinalalapag" ("lay down/land"), which cuts the link to error propagation, the page's main theme. "Classically detect" is also rendered "itinutukoy" ("point to"). Smaller problems: "necessitates" in [36] becomes "nagpapailalim" ("subjects to"), [64] has the ungrammatical "medyo ng aksidente", and there are typos: "napakahalgang" [4], "magpalat" [8] and "bawisa" [16].

examples.source: for measuring stabilizer generators non-destructively using phase estimation
examples.translation: para sa pagsukat ng mga stabilizer generator nang hindi mapanganib gamit ang phase estimation
examples.suggested: para sa pagsukat ng mga stabilizer generator nang hindi sinisira ang state (non-destructively) gamit ang phase estimation
examples.why: 'hindi mapanganib' means 'not dangerous/harmless'. That is not what non-destructive measurement means, so the learner is taught the wrong concept.

examples.source: we *intentionally* propagate errors to a workspace system, and then measure that system and *classically* detect errors
examples.translation: *sadya nating* pinalalapag ang mga error sa isang workspace system, at pagkatapos ay sinusukat ang system na iyon at *classically* itinutukoy ang mga error
examples.suggested: *sadya nating* pinakakalat ang mga error papunta sa isang workspace system, at pagkatapos ay sinusukat ang system na iyon at *classically* dine-detect ang mga error
examples.why: The page renders 'propagate' as 'kalat' everywhere else. 'pinalalapag' ('lay down') hides that Steane EC deliberately uses error propagation, and 'itinutukoy' ('point to') is not 'detect'.

examples.source: which necessitates the use of alternative gadgets
examples.translation: na nagpapailalim sa paggamit ng mga alternatibong gadget
examples.suggested: kaya kailangang gumamit ng mga alternatibong gadget
examples.why: 'nagpapailalim' means 'subjects to/places under', not 'necessitates'. The causal point gets muddled.

examples.source: remarkably and somewhat coincidentally
examples.translation: kahanga-hanga at medyo ng aksidente
examples.suggested: kapansin-pansin, at medyo nagkataon lamang
examples.why: This is ungrammatical and reads like raw machine translation.

examples.source: each depicted as consisting of five qubits
examples.translation: bawisa ay inilalarawan na binubuo ng limang qubit
examples.suggested: bawat isa ay inilalarawang binubuo ng limang qubit
examples.why: Typo: 'bawisa' should be 'bawat isa'. Similar typos appear in [4] ('napakahalgang') and [8] ('magpalat').

editor_note: The page is mostly faithful and nothing in it would mislead a learner, but a few phrasings are off. In [35], "finitely many" becomes "natapos na bilang" ("finished/completed number") where it should be "may hangganang bilang", and "happen to be real numbers" softens to "maaaring maging mga tunay na numero" ("can be"). In [40], "unique up to the ordering" is calqued as "natatangi hanggang sa pagkakasunod" ("until the ordering"), although [14] correctly uses "maliban sa" for "up to". In [62], "maaaring kaya ay aalisin" is ungrammatical. Measurement is split between "sukat" (which reads as size/measure; "pagsukat" is more natural) and the English "measurement" in compounds.

examples.source: because matrices have only finitely many eigenvalues, there will only be finitely many different measurement outcomes
examples.translation: dahil ang mga matrix ay mayroon lamang natapos na bilang ng mga eigenvalue, magkakaroon lamang ng natapos na bilang ng iba't ibang kinalabasan
examples.suggested: dahil may hangganang bilang lamang ng eigenvalue ang mga matrix, may hangganang bilang lamang din ng magkakaibang kinalabasan
examples.why: 'natapos' means finished or completed, not finite. The mathematical sense is 'may hangganan'.

examples.source: So, the outcomes for such a measurement happen to be real numbers
examples.translation: Kaya, ang mga kinalabasan para sa ganitong sukat ay maaaring maging mga tunay na numero
examples.suggested: Kaya, mga tunay na numero ang mga kinalabasan ng ganitong pagsukat
examples.why: 'maaaring maging' (can be) softens the statement, but eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix are always real.

examples.source: Such an expression of a matrix is unique up to the ordering of the eigenvalues.
examples.translation: Ang ganitong expression ng isang matrix ay natatangi hanggang sa pagkakasunod ng mga eigenvalue.
examples.suggested: Natatangi ang ganitong expression ng isang matrix, maliban sa pagkakasunod ng mga eigenvalue.
examples.why: 'hanggang sa' is a literal calque of 'up to' and reads as 'until'. Entry [14] already uses the correct 'maliban sa'.

examples.source: controlled-identity gates are simply identity gates and can therefore be omitted
examples.translation: ang mga controlled-identity gate ay simpleng mga identity gate at maaaring kaya ay aalisin
examples.suggested: identity gate lang talaga ang mga controlled-identity gate, kaya puwede na itong alisin
examples.why: 'maaaring kaya ay aalisin' is ungrammatical word salad.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The core claims, that G is a rotation by 2θ, that two reflections make a rotation, and that swapping f for g changes only the global phase, are faithful and would not mislead a learner. Some wording still needs an editor. In [81], "which we're assuming" became "na inaasahan nating" ("which we expect"), where "ipinapalagay" is the right verb. "Reflection about the line" is calqued as "reflection tungkol sa linya" in [81] and [85]. "So far in this series" became "Sa ngayon" ("for now") in [54], and "therefore" was dropped in [37]. The double negative "hindi walang laman" in [9] and [10] reads stiffly where "may laman" would be natural.

examples.source: which we're assuming is a real linear combination of |A0> and |A1>
examples.translation: na inaasahan nating isang tunay na linear combination
examples.suggested: na ipinapalagay nating isang tunay na linear combination
examples.why: 'inaasahan' means 'expect', not 'assume'. It turns a stated assumption into an expectation.

examples.source: a reflection about the line parallel to |A0>
examples.translation: isang reflection tungkol sa linya na parallel sa |A0>
examples.suggested: isang reflection sa linya na parallel sa |A0>
examples.why: 'tungkol sa' means 'regarding a topic'. Using it for a geometric 'about' is a calque, and the same calque appears in [85].

examples.source: So far in this series, we've always connected...
examples.translation: Sa ngayon sa seryeng ito, palagi tayong nag-uugnay...
examples.suggested: Hanggang ngayon sa seryeng ito, palagi nating iniuugnay...
examples.why: 'Sa ngayon' reads as 'for now', not 'up to this point'.

examples.source: we're going to focus on the case that neither A0 nor A1 is empty
examples.translation: magtutuon tayo sa kasong hindi walang laman ang $A_0$ at $A_1$
examples.suggested: magtutuon tayo sa kasong parehong may laman ang $A_0$ at $A_1$
examples.why: The double negative 'hindi walang laman' is stiff translationese. 'May laman' is the natural phrasing, and the same issue appears in [10].

examples.source: The operation ... can therefore be written like this:
examples.translation: Ang operation na ... ay maaaring isulat nang ganito:
examples.suggested: Kaya, ang operation na ... ay maaaring isulat nang ganito:
examples.why: 'Therefore' was dropped, which loses the signal that this result follows from the previous expression.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing here would mislead a learner. The search procedure, the Z_f/Z_OR cost comparison and the t = O(√N) claim all match the source. A few stretches read as calqued or ungrammatical Tagalog. [23] and [32] use the actor-focus "maaari tayong" with object-focus verbs ("maaari tayong makatwirang asahan", "maaari tayong muling patakbuhin"). [33] uses the Taglish calque "sa pag-take ng" and renders "probability" as "posibilidad". [16] glosses "dependensya" as "(pag-asa)", which reads as "hope". [24] renders "measurements" as "mga sukat", which reads as "sizes", even though [20] uses "measurement".

examples.source: we can reasonably expect that the resulting quantum circuit will be larger
examples.translation: maaari tayong makatwirang asahan na ang resultang quantum circuit ay magiging mas malaki
examples.suggested: makatwiran nating maaasahan na mas malaki ang magiging resultang quantum circuit
examples.why: Actor-focus 'tayo' paired with object-focus 'asahan' is ungrammatical, and the phrasing is calqued from English.

examples.source: then we can either run the procedure again
examples.translation: maaari tayong muling patakbuhin ang pamamaraan
examples.suggested: maaari nating patakbuhin muli ang pamamaraan
examples.why: Wrong pronoun focus: object-focus 'patakbuhin' needs 'natin', not 'tayo'.

examples.source: by taking $t = O(\sqrt{N})$, we obtain a solution ... with high probability
examples.translation: sa pag-take ng $t = O(\sqrt{N})$ ... nang may mataas na posibilidad
examples.suggested: kung pipiliin nating $t = O(\sqrt{N})$ ... nang may mataas na probabilidad
examples.why: 'pag-take' is a Taglish calque. 'posibilidad' means possibility, not the technical 'probability'.

examples.source: has no dependence on the function $f$
examples.translation: walang dependensya (pag-asa) sa function na $f$
examples.suggested: hindi nakadepende sa function na $f$
examples.why: The parenthetical gloss 'pag-asa' reads as 'hope' and makes the sentence clumsy.

examples.source: immediately before the measurements
examples.translation: agad bago ang mga sukat
examples.suggested: bago mismo ang mga measurement
examples.why: 'sukat' reads as 'size/dimension'. It is also inconsistent with 'standard basis measurement' in [20].

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The complexity claims (N, O(N), O(√N)), the promise and non-promise problems, and the Or problem all match the English. The word choices are the problem. 'Solves' is always rendered with the Spanish-derived 'nireresolta' where native Tagalog would use 'nilulutas'. Entry [9] mixes 'komplikadong' and 'napakacomplex' in two sentences in a row, and uses the same verb 'suriin/pagsusuri' for both 'examining' and 'evaluating' the circuit, which muddies the distinction the English draws between the two. 'Evaluations/iterations' stay as English plurals after 'na' in [12]/[13], and 'satisfying f(x)=1' in [20] is rendered as 'tumutugon sa' ('responds to').

examples.source: we have no hope of making sense of the circuit by examining it (beyond having the ability to evaluate it on selected input strings)
examples.translation: wala tayong pagkakataon na maunawaan ito sa pamamagitan ng pagsusuri nito (bukod sa kakayahang suriin ito sa mga napiling input string)
examples.suggested: ...sa pamamagitan ng pagsisiyasat nito (bukod sa kakayahang i-evaluate ito sa mga napiling input string)
examples.why: The same root (suri) is used for both 'examine' and 'evaluate', which blurs the contrast between inspecting the circuit and running it. The sentence before it also mixes 'komplikadong' and 'napakacomplex'.

examples.source: the problem that Grover's algorithm solves
examples.translation: ng problema na nireresolta ng algorithm ni Grover
examples.suggested: ng problemang nilulutas ng algorithm ni Grover
examples.why: 'Nireresolta' is a stiff Spanish-derived calque. 'Nilulutas' is the natural Tagalog verb for solving a problem. The same issue repeats in [13], [15] and [18].

examples.source: a string $x\in\Sigma^n$ satisfying $f(x) = 1$
examples.translation: isang string $x\in\Sigma^n$ na tumutugon sa $f(x) = 1$
examples.suggested: isang string $x\in\Sigma^n$ na nagbibigay ng $f(x) = 1$
examples.why: 'Tumutugon sa' reads as 'responds to'. That is an awkward way to say a string satisfies a condition.

editor_note: The final argument for why order finding splits N is garbled in [161]. "So long as" becomes "hanggang sa" ("until"), and "prime factors divide the term" becomes "hahatiin sa unang termino", which reverses who divides whom. In [126], "v must at least divide r" becomes "dapat na hindi bababa sa hatiin ang r", which reads like a size bound on v ("not less than") rather than divisibility. [153]'s "neither of these events happen" is also weakened to an ambiguous "ang alinman ... ay hindi nangyayari". Smaller fixes: "satisfy" is rendered throughout as "sumasaklaw sa" ("covers"), [157] has "matapos nating tapusin na", and there are typos "pinagtatarabahong" [14] and "boundna" [142].

examples.source: Otherwise, so long as some of the prime factors of $N$ divide the first term and some divide the second term, we'll be able to find a non-trivial factor of $N$ by computing the GCD with the first term.
examples.translation: Kung hindi, hanggang sa ilang prime factor ng $N$ ang hahatiin sa unang termino at ang ilan ay hahatiin sa pangalawang termino, malalaman natin ang isang non-trivial na factor ng $N$...
examples.suggested: Kung hindi, basta't may ilang prime factor ng $N$ na naghahati sa unang termino at may ilan na naghahati sa pangalawang termino, makakahanap tayo ng non-trivial na factor ng $N$ sa pamamagitan ng pagkalkula ng GCD nito sa unang termino.
examples.why: 'hanggang sa' means 'until', not 'so long as'. 'hahatiin sa' makes the prime factor the thing being divided, so both the condition and the divisibility relation that carry the key argument are wrong.

examples.source: the number $v$ we obtain from the continued fraction algorithm must at least divide $r$.
examples.translation: ang bilang na $v$ na nakukuha natin mula sa continued fraction algorithm ay dapat na hindi bababa sa hatiin ang $r$.
examples.suggested: ang bilang na $v$ na nakukuha natin mula sa continued fraction algorithm ay tiyak na naghahati man lang sa $r$ (ibig sabihin, ang $v$ ay divisor ng $r$).
examples.why: 'hindi bababa sa' is the quantitative 'not less than', so a reader could take it as v ≥ r instead of 'v is a divisor of r'. That is exactly why the lesson goes on to take the LCM of the observed denominators.

examples.source: for a random choice of $a$, with probability at least $1/2$ neither of these events happen.
examples.translation: na may probabilidad na hindi bababa sa $1/2$ ang alinman sa mga pangyayaring ito ay hindi nangyayari.
examples.suggested: na may probabilidad na hindi bababa sa $1/2$, wala sa dalawang pangyayaring ito ang nangyayari.
examples.why: 'ang alinman ... ay hindi nangyayari' can be read as 'at least one of them doesn't happen', which is weaker than 'neither happens'.

examples.source: the elements $a\in\mathbb{Z}_N$ that satisfy $\gcd(a,N) = 1$
examples.translation: ang mga elemento na $a\in\mathbb{Z}_N$ na sumasaklaw sa $\gcd(a,N) = 1$
examples.suggested: ang mga elementong $a\in\mathbb{Z}_N$ na tumutugon sa kondisyong $\gcd(a,N) = 1$
examples.why: 'sumasaklaw' means 'covers/encompasses', not the mathematical 'satisfies'. The same wording is used in [29], [37], [106], [113] and [122].

examples.source: Using the formula $Z^2 - 1 = (Z+1)(Z-1)$, we conclude that
examples.translation: Gamit ang formula na $Z^2 - 1 = (Z+1)(Z-1)$, matapos nating tapusin na
examples.suggested: Gamit ang formula na $Z^2 - 1 = (Z+1)(Z-1)$, mahihinuha natin na
examples.why: 'matapos nating tapusin' means 'after we finish', a mistranslation of 'conclude' that breaks the logical step.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The page does have several phrasing slips a native editor would fix. In [24], "natuklasan na sana nito" uses "nito" where "by now" needs "ngayon", and "huwag mong inaasahan" should be the imperative "huwag mong asahan". The GCD definition in [21], "pantay na hinahati ang kapwa", is a stiff calque of "evenly divides both". Other slips: "kahit paano sa aming kaalaman" [15] for "at least as far as we know", "dose-dosenang libong makina" [17] for "tens of thousands of machines", and a few dropped qualifiers ("seems", "inherently", "considerably").

examples.source: would have been discovered by now ... but don't hold your breath
examples.translation: ay natuklasan na sana nito ... ngunit huwag mong inaasahan
examples.suggested: ay natuklasan na sana ngayon ... pero huwag kang umasa / huwag mong asahan
examples.why: 'nito' (of it) is wrong for 'by now', and a negative imperative takes the base form 'asahan', not the progressive 'inaasahan'.

examples.source: the largest integer that evenly divides both of them
examples.translation: ang pinakamalaking integer na pantay na hinahati ang kapwa
examples.suggested: ang pinakamalaking integer na eksaktong naghahati (walang natitira) sa dalawang numero
examples.why: 'pantay na hinahati ang kapwa' is a literal calque. 'Evenly divides' means dividing with no remainder, and a key definition should say that clearly.

examples.source: things become impossibly difficult, at least as far as we know
examples.translation: nagiging imposible ang mga bagay, kahit paano sa aming kaalaman
examples.suggested: nagiging imposibleng mahirap ito, sa abot ng ating nalalaman
examples.why: 'kahit paano' means 'somehow/anyway', not 'at least', and exclusive 'aming' leaves out the reader. The inclusive 'ating' fits better.

examples.source: distributed across tens of thousands of machines
examples.translation: na ipinamamahagi sa dose-dosenang libong makina
examples.suggested: na ipinamahagi sa sampu-sampung libong makina
examples.why: 'Tens of thousands' is conventionally 'sampu-sampung libo'. Also, the present tense 'ipinamamahagi' doesn't fit a computation that finished in 2020.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall, and the garbage/uncompute argument and the invertible-function caveat in [51] come through intact. There are several local defects a native editor would fix. In [17], "the qubits that the gates act upon" becomes "kinakatawanan ng" ("represented by"), which is also misspelled. In [32], intransitive "masira" makes the garbage qubits the thing that breaks, not the thing that breaks the interference patterns. In [29], "short for garbage" becomes "paikling termino para sa *basura*", so the g-for-garbage pun no longer works, and "nagmamalasakit" is the wrong sense of "care". Smaller slips: "so to speak" is rendered "sa madaling sabi" ("in short") in [33], and "nagXO-or" in [49] is garbled.

examples.source: the qubits that the AND, OR, and FANOUT gates act upon come in from the left as inputs
examples.translation: ang mga qubit na kinakatawanan ng mga AND, OR, at FANOUT gate ay pumapasok mula sa kaliwa
examples.suggested: ang mga qubit na pinag-aaksyunan ng mga AND, OR, at FANOUT gate ay pumapasok mula sa kaliwa
examples.why: 'Represented by' is not the same as 'acted upon', and 'kinakatawanan' is a misspelling of 'kinakatawan'. The context about inputs keeps it from misleading much.

examples.source: garbage qubits can ruin the interference patterns
examples.translation: ang mga garbage qubit ay maaaring masira ang mga interference pattern
examples.suggested: ang mga garbage qubit ay maaaring sumira sa mga interference pattern
examples.why: 'Masira' is intransitive (to get broken), so the sentence is ungrammatical and reads as if the qubits themselves break.

examples.source: we don't care specifically what state ... it's short for *garbage.*
examples.translation: hindi tayo nagmamalasakit kung anong estado ... ito ay paikling termino para sa *basura.*
examples.suggested: wala tayong pakialam kung anong estado talaga ... ito ay maikli para sa *garbage* (basura).
examples.why: 'G' is not short for 'basura', so the naming joke falls apart unless the English word is kept. 'Nagmamalasakit' means caring in the compassionate sense.

examples.source: it's not difficult to clean up the garbage, so to speak.
examples.translation: hindi mahirap linisin ang basura, sa madaling sabi.
examples.suggested: hindi mahirap linisin ang basura, kung baga.
examples.why: 'Sa madaling sabi' means 'in short', not 'so to speak'.

examples.source: XORing it to an arbitrary string
examples.translation: nagXO-or ito sa isang arbitrary na string
examples.suggested: nag-XOR nito sa isang arbitrary na string
examples.why: The verb form is garbled and hyphenated wrongly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The OR, Parity, Minimum and Unique-search definitions, the "don't care" promise caveat, and the claim that U_f is its own inverse and a permutation matrix all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. What a native editor would change is calqued or stiff phrasing. "Shortly" is rendered as "sa lalong madaling panahon" ("as soon as possible"), which appears twice. Entry [24] keeps English syntax in "Hindi ito nangangahulugang ... bagaman!" and has the ungrammatical "may sinuman ay talagang gustong". There are also smaller slips: exclusive "aming pinipili" where it should be inclusive "ating", the non-standard "isulatin", the half-English "nasatisfied", and "at all" dropped in [24].

examples.source: with some simple examples described shortly
examples.translation: na may ilang simpleng halimbawa na inilalarawan sa lalong madaling panahon
examples.suggested: na may ilang simpleng halimbawang ilalarawan maya-maya
examples.why: 'sa lalong madaling panahon' means 'as soon as possible', which is an idiom calque. It also recurs in [13]. The same entry uses the non-standard 'isulatin' where 'isulat' is correct.

examples.source: where it's difficult to imagine that anyone would ever actually want to solve them in practice. This doesn't mean that the problems aren't interesting, though!
examples.translation: mahirap isipin na may sinuman ay talagang gustong lutasin ang mga ito sa practice. Hindi ito nangangahulugang ang mga problema ay hindi kawili-wili, bagaman!
examples.suggested: mahirap isiping may sinumang talagang gugustuhing lutasin ang mga ito sa praktika. Pero hindi ibig sabihin nito na hindi na kawili-wili ang mga problemang ito!
examples.why: 'may sinuman ay' is ungrammatical, and ending the sentence with 'bagaman!' copies the English 'though!' word for word.

examples.source: we can only evaluate it on arguments we select
examples.translation: maaari lang nating e-evaluate ito sa mga argumento na aming pinipili
examples.suggested: maaari lang natin itong i-evaluate sa mga argumentong ating pinipili
examples.why: The exclusive 'amin' clashes with the inclusive 'natin' used in the same clause, and 'e-evaluate' should be 'i-evaluate'.

examples.source: the ones for which the promise is not satisfied
examples.translation: ang mga kung saan hindi nasatisfied ang promise
examples.suggested: iyong mga hindi tumutupad sa promise
examples.why: 'nasatisfied' is an awkward half-English form, and 'ang mga kung saan' copies the English relative clause.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The coordinates, the pole/equator explanations, the caveat about when theta and phi are unique, and the Bloch-ball discussion all match the English, and the casual register holds. The problems are word choice. "trigonometric identities" becomes "trigonometric na pagkakatulad" (resemblances). "Pole" in [21] becomes "poste" (a post or pillar), while the rest of the file keeps "north pole" and "south pole". In [6], "allowing theta to range" is rendered with "lumayo" (to go far away). [52] also has a grammar slip: "mga puntong *loob*" is missing "sa".

examples.source: We can use some trigonometric identities,
examples.translation: Maaari tayong gumamit ng ilang trigonometric na pagkakatulad,
examples.suggested: Maaari tayong gumamit ng ilang trigonometric identity,
examples.why: 'pagkakatulad' means similarity or resemblance, not a mathematical identity. The term is still recognizable, but it is imprecise.

examples.source: the curve on the surface of the sphere from one pole to the other
examples.translation: ang kurba sa ibabaw ng sphere mula sa isang poste hanggang sa isa pa
examples.suggested: ang kurba sa ibabaw ng sphere mula sa isang pole hanggang sa kabilang pole
examples.why: 'poste' means a physical post or pillar, not a geographic pole. It also clashes with the 'north pole' and 'south pole' used elsewhere in the file.

examples.source: we're allowing θ to range from 0 to π
examples.translation: pinayagan nating lumayo ang θ mula 0 hanggang π
examples.suggested: hinahayaan nating sumaklaw ang θ mula 0 hanggang π
examples.why: 'lumayo' means to move far away. It is a poor calque of 'range' in a parameter-domain sense.

examples.source: this results in points *inside* of the Bloch sphere
examples.translation: nagreresulta ito sa mga puntong *loob* ng Bloch sphere
examples.suggested: nagreresulta ito sa mga punto sa *loob* ng Bloch sphere
examples.why: The locative 'sa' is missing, so the phrase is ungrammatical.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The Bob light-years argument in [42], the separable/entangled definitions and the partial-trace formulas all match the English, with no inverted or dropped claims. Several sentences are garbled or read as calques. "Pagtutulad ng nang sa" in [51] and "mayroon tayong na may probabilidad" in [25] are ungrammatical. "Inilalagay sa pagsusulatan" in [5] uses "pagsusulatan", which means writing letters to each other, not mathematical correspondence. "Nagbibigay-kasiyahan sa mga formula" in [75] literally means "gives pleasure to", not "satisfies". Other slips: *kalayaan* ("freedom") for statistical independence in [14], "at katotohanan" in [27], "natutalakay lamang" in [45] and "nangyayaring ding" in [43].

examples.source: Reasoning similarly to the previous example of an e-bit, if we were to measure the system B
examples.translation: Pagtutulad ng nang sa nakaraang halimbawa ng e-bit, kung susukat tayo ng sistema B
examples.suggested: Gamit ang katulad na pangangatwiran sa nakaraang halimbawa ng e-bit, kung susukatin natin ang sistemang B
examples.why: The opening words are ungrammatical, and 'susukat tayo ng' is the wrong verb focus.

examples.source: we have that with probability p_k the system on the left is in the state ρ_k
examples.translation: mayroon tayong na may probabilidad na p_k ang sistema sa kaliwa ay nasa estado
examples.suggested: may probabilidad na p_k na ang sistema sa kaliwa ay nasa estadong ρ_k
examples.why: 'We have that' is copied word for word from English, which leaves the sentence broken.

examples.source: are placed in correspondence with the Cartesian product
examples.translation: ay inilalagay sa pagsusulatan sa Cartesian product
examples.suggested: ay itinutugma sa Cartesian product
examples.why: 'Pagsusulatan' means writing letters to each other, not a mathematical correspondence. Elsewhere the file correctly uses 'tumutugma'.

examples.source: the unique linear mappings that satisfy the formulas
examples.translation: ang natatanging linear mapping na nagbibigay-kasiyahan sa mga formula
examples.suggested: ang natatanging linear mapping na tumutugon sa mga formula
examples.why: 'Nagbibigay-kasiyahan' means 'pleases'. It is a literal calque of 'satisfy', which is wrong in a math context.

examples.source: tensor products of density matrices represent *independence*
examples.translation: kumakatawan sa *kalayaan* sa pagitan ng mga estado
examples.suggested: kumakatawan sa *pagiging independiyente* ng mga estado
examples.why: 'Kalayaan' means freedom or liberty. It does not carry the sense of statistical independence, and it is the emphasized key concept of this paragraph.

editor_note: The meaning holds overall and the terms are consistent (measurement→sukat, unitary operation, Stinespring representation, "nakatali sa" for "conditioned on"). A few grammar slips and calques bend the sense locally. [3] "Ang sistema na susukat" uses actor focus, so it reads as the system doing the measuring; it should be "susukatin". [39] renders "So far… we've concerned ourselves" as "Sa ngayon… pag-aabalahin natin" ("for now… we will concern ourselves"), which loses the backward look. [58] "palitan ang (I⊗V)U para sa U" copies the English "substitute A for B" word for word, and in Tagalog it reads as replacing (I⊗V)U. Entry [60] gets the pattern right with "palitan ang U ng…". Smaller slips: "Konkretamente" [40], "maaari tayong punan" [26], the missing verb in "posibleng higit pang pangkalahatan" [42], "para sa Q^2 = P" [14] and "may kahulugan kung saan" [43].

examples.source: The system to be measured is first combined with an initialized workspace system
examples.translation: Ang sistema na susukat ay unang pinagsama sa isang initialized na workspace system
examples.suggested: Ang sistemang susukatin ay unang pinagsasama sa isang initialized na workspace system
examples.why: 'susukat' is actor focus, so it means 'the system that will measure'. The object-focus form 'susukatin' is needed, and 'pinagsama' should be present tense to match the numbered steps.

examples.source: So far in the lesson, we've concerned ourselves with *destructive* measurements
examples.translation: Sa ngayon sa aralin, pag-aabalahin natin ang mga *destructive* na sukat
examples.suggested: Hanggang ngayon sa aralin, ang pinagtuunan natin ay ang mga *destructive* na sukat
examples.why: The English looks back at what the lesson has covered. The translation uses the future tense ('we will concern ourselves'), which suggests this section is about destructive measurements when it actually introduces non-destructive ones.

examples.source: one option is to substitute $(\mathbb{I}_{\mathsf{Y}} \otimes V) U$ for $U$
examples.translation: isang opsyon ay palitan ang $(\mathbb{I}_{\mathsf{Y}} \otimes V) U$ para sa $U$
examples.suggested: isang opsyon ay palitan ang $U$ ng $(\mathbb{I}_{\mathsf{Y}} \otimes V) U$
examples.why: This copies 'substitute A for B' word for word. In Tagalog, 'palitan ang A' means A is the thing being replaced, so the direction reads backwards. Entry [60] already uses the correct pattern.

examples.source: Specifically, non-destructive measurements describe not only…
examples.translation: Konkretamente, inilalarawan ng mga non-destructive na sukat…
examples.suggested: Partikular, inilalarawan ng mga non-destructive na sukat…
examples.why: 'Konkretamente' is a Spanish form, not standard Tagalog. Also, 'ginagawa nang tiyak ang bagay na ito' in the preceding sentence is stiff.

examples.source: It is, in fact, possible to generalize non-destructive measurements even further
examples.translation: Sa katunayan, posibleng higit pang pangkalahatan ang mga non-destructive na sukat
examples.suggested: Sa katunayan, posibleng gawing mas pangkalahatan pa ang mga non-destructive na sukat
examples.why: The verb is missing: 'pangkalahatan' is a noun or adjective, so the sentence does not say 'generalize'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The bond-length and energy targets (0.74 Angstrom, -1.17 Hartrees) and the point that only the hardware run used error mitigation both survive intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix three things. Entry [7] opens with the non-word "Ostaying", which should be "Manatili". Entry [22] renders "and indeed it is close" as the stiff "at katotohanan na malapit ito". Entry [24] uses the calqued negation "hindi malamang na mapabuti" where "malamang na hindi mapapabuti" is the natural word order.

examples.source: Remaining with our basic example of diatomic hydrogen
examples.translation: Ostaying sa ating pangunahing halimbawa ng diatomic hydrogen
examples.suggested: Manatili tayo sa ating pangunahing halimbawa ng diatomic hydrogen
examples.why: 'Ostaying' is not a Tagalog word. It looks like a garbled mix of English and Tagalog in the page's opening sentence.

examples.source: and indeed it is close
examples.translation: at katotohanan na malapit ito
examples.suggested: at totoo ngang malapit ito
examples.why: 'katotohanan na' is a literal, stiff rendering of 'indeed'. The emphatic particle 'nga' is the natural way to say it.

examples.source: is not likely to improve the results
examples.translation: ay hindi malamang na mapabuti ang mga resulta
examples.suggested: ay malamang na hindi mapapabuti ang mga resulta
examples.why: This copies the English order of the negation. Native Tagalog puts the negation after 'malamang' ('malamang na hindi'), which reads more clearly.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: the 50/50 statistics, the X expectation value of 1, the H-H cancellation, the -y result and the caveat that measurement is the only source of randomness are all rendered correctly. The problems are grammar and word choice. [56] has 'kapag sinukat tayo' ('when we are measured') where it needs 'kapag sinukat natin'. [125] uses 'paikot-ikot' where it needs 'pinaiikot'. [127] has the non-word 'paratanggap' where it needs 'diumano'y'. There are also typos: 'hahara' in [57], 'paligaan' in [93] and 'Kabila ng' in [25]. Terms are split within the file: 'heads' is both 'ulo' and 'mukha'; 'coefficient' is both 'koepisyente' and 'coefficient'; 'imaginary part' is 'haka-hakang bahagi' in [24] but 'imaginary' in [63]. Complex coefficients are called 'kumplikado' ('complicated') in [24] and [63].

examples.source: we have 100% probability of measuring the state $|+\rangle$ when we measure along X.
examples.translation: ibig sabihin ay 100% ang posibilidad ng pagsukat ng estado $|+\rangle$ kapag sinukat tayo sa kahabaan ng X.
examples.suggested: ibig sabihin ay 100% ang posibilidad na masukat natin ang estado $|+\rangle$ kapag sumukat tayo sa kahabaan ng X.
examples.why: 'sinukat tayo' makes 'we' the thing being measured, which is a grammar error. Context still carries the meaning.

examples.source: Quantum gates rotate this coin/Bloch vector deterministically and reversibly. It is only when we **measure** the qubit that any randomness is introduced.
examples.translation: Ang mga Quantum gate ay paikot-ikot ang barya/Bloch vector na ito nang deterministiko at reversible. Kapag **sinukat** natin ang qubit lamang naipasok ang anumang randomness.
examples.suggested: Pinaiikot ng mga quantum gate ang barya/Bloch vector na ito nang deterministiko at reversible. Kapag **sinukat** lamang natin ang qubit saka pumapasok ang randomness.
examples.why: 'paikot-ikot' is an adverb/adjective ('round and round'), not a transitive verb, and the 'only when' clause is clumsily ordered.

examples.source: one of the supposedly "weirdest" aspects
examples.translation: ang isa sa mga paratanggap na "pinaka-kakaibang" aspeto
examples.suggested: ang isa sa mga diumano'y "pinaka-kakaibang" aspeto
examples.why: 'paratanggap' is not a Tagalog word. 'Supposedly' is diumano'y or sinasabing.

examples.source: each of these coefficients can now be complex, meaning they can have both real and imaginary parts.
examples.translation: ang bawat isa sa mga koepisyenteng ito ay maaaring maging kumplikado na ngayon, ibig sabihin, maaari silang magkaroon ng parehong tunay at haka-hakang bahagi.
examples.suggested: ang bawat isa sa mga coefficient na ito ay maaari nang maging complex, ibig sabihin, may real at imaginary na bahagi.
examples.why: 'kumplikado' reads as 'complicated', and 'haka-haka' means 'speculative'. Entry [63] uses 'imaginary' and 'coefficient', so the file is split between two renderings.

examples.source: we will soon see that there is much more to it than that.
examples.translation: mabilis nating makikita na may mas maraming ito kaysa doon.
examples.suggested: makikita natin sa lalong madaling panahon na higit pa rito ang superposition.
examples.why: This is a word-for-word calque and ungrammatical. 'Soon' has also turned into 'mabilis' ('quickly').

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The sampling overhead of 9^3, the "more than half" depth reduction and the swap counts are all kept. "Decompose" is rendered three ways ("pagbubukod"/"nabukod" in [10] and [23], "bubuuin" in [20]). "Bubuuin", meaning "to build", reads closer to "compose" than "decompose", so "hatiin" would be clearer. In [24], "shallower" became "mas mababa" ("lower") instead of the file's own "mas mababaw". The heading "Pinagmulan" ("origin") for "Background" is also slightly off; "Konteksto" would fit better.

examples.source: how to decompose the cut gates into single-qubit operations
examples.translation: kung paano bubuuin ang mga pinutol na gate sa mga single-qubit operation
examples.suggested: kung paano hahatiin ang mga pinutol na gate sa mga single-qubit operation
examples.why: 'Bubuuin' means build/compose, which runs against 'decompose'. It also clashes with 'pagbubukod'/'nabukod' used for the same term in [10] and [23].

examples.source: the QPD subexperiments will be shallower after cutting distant gates
examples.translation: ang mga QPD subexperiment ay magiging mas mababa pagkatapos ng pagputol
examples.suggested: ang mga QPD subexperiment ay magiging mas mababaw pagkatapos ng pagputol
examples.why: 'Mas mababa' means 'lower', not 'shallower'. Everywhere else the file uses 'mas mababaw' for circuit depth.

examples.source: Background
examples.translation: Pinagmulan
examples.suggested: Konteksto
examples.why: 'Pinagmulan' means origin/source. It isn't the usual word for a 'Background' section heading.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall and nothing in it would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix a few slips. [47] turns "pretty good estimation" into "napakahusay na estimate" ("excellent estimate"), which overstates the claim. [10] renders "interleaved with" as "pinagsasama sa" ("combined with"), so the alternating layer structure gets lost. [50] uses "Tatawagan" (to phone someone) where calling a function needs "tatawagin". The title [1] leaves the verb as bare "Simulate ang" instead of "I-simulate ang", and [12] "sa halaga ng" is a calque of "at the cost of".

examples.source: gives a pretty good estimation and uses a few minutes of QPU time
examples.translation: nagbibigay ng napakahusay na estimate
examples.suggested: nagbibigay ng medyo mahusay na estimate
examples.why: 'pretty good' is a moderate claim, but 'napakahusay' means excellent, so the accuracy of the empirical estimate is overstated.

examples.source: interleaved with layers of single-qubit gates
examples.translation: na pinagsasama sa mga layers ng single-qubit gates
examples.suggested: na sinasalitan ng mga layers ng single-qubit gates
examples.why: 'pinagsasama' means combined, which loses the alternating (interleaved) layer structure of the Trotter step.

examples.source: We call the function:
examples.translation: Tatawagan natin ang function:
examples.suggested: Tatawagin natin ang function:
examples.why: 'tatawagan' means to phone someone. Calling a function is 'tatawagin'.

examples.source: Simulate 2D tilted-field Ising with the QESEM function
examples.translation: Simulate ang 2D tilted-field Ising gamit ang QESEM function
examples.suggested: I-simulate ang 2D tilted-field Ising gamit ang QESEM function
examples.why: The English verb is left without the i- affix, so the title is ungrammatical. The body text uses 'i-simulate' correctly.

examples.source: at the cost of more operator measurements
examples.translation: sa halaga ng mas maraming operator measurements
examples.suggested: kapalit ng mas maraming operator measurements
examples.why: 'sa halaga ng' is a literal calque. 'kapalit ng' is the natural way to express a trade-off.
